title: Postgres: running the same job twice
summary: Runs the pg_apache_logs batch job twice on an unchanged folder and checks whether the second run skips the files already processed or loads everything again (duplicate rows). It may legitimately fail: the pipeline is configured as full_refresh with append writes.

steps.title: Empty the apache_logs table
steps.explain: Starts from nothing so run 1 is a true first run.

steps.title: Count source files
steps.explain: The number of files a fresh run should read.

steps.title: Read sample rows (Before)
steps.explain: Shows the table is empty before run 1.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, sequence_index, left(text, 50) AS text_start FROM apache_logs ORDER BY source_filename, sequence_index LIMIT 5

steps.title: Run the same job again, nothing changed
steps.explain: The question: does OpenETL remember the files it already processed?

steps.title: Count rows after run 2
steps.explain: Compared with run 1 to detect duplicates.

steps.title: Run 1 COMPLETED
steps.explain: Confirms the first load itself worked.

steps.title: Run 2 reports 0 files processed
steps.explain: If state tracking worked, an unchanged folder yields no new files.

steps.title: Run 2 reports 0 records
steps.explain: No new files should mean no new records.

steps.title: Row count after run 2 equals run 1
steps.explain: More rows means the second run loaded everything twice.

steps.title: Count extra rows (total minus distinct lines)
steps.explain: Identical rows repeated by the second run.

args.sql: SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT (source_filename, sequence_index)) FROM apache_logs

steps.title: No chunk is stored twice
steps.explain: Duplicates after a rerun are the visible damage.

steps.title: Read sample rows (After)
steps.explain: Shows the table after both runs.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, sequence_index, left(text, 50) AS text_start FROM apache_logs ORDER BY source_filename, sequence_index LIMIT 5
